gospel: matthew 22:34.40as we approach the month of november, the church invites us to remember in a special way those who gone before us in faith. praying for our deceased l oved ones is one of the beautiful traditions of our cath olic faith, reminding us that the bonds of love are not broken by death. as in previous years, i invite you to write the names of your deceased family members and friends o n the november dead lists and place them in the envelopes provided at the front of the church. throughout november, at every mass, we will remembe r all those whose names have been entrusted to our prayers. each envelope will be opened, the names read and placed upon the altar, a beautiful reminder that those we love are never forgotten, either by us or by god. on another note, it was a real joy to host a dioces an women's discernment evening here in st colmcille's on thursday evening. twenty young women gathered to reflect and pray about what god might be calling them to, particularly the possibility of religious life. it was wonderful to see such openness and generosity o f spirit. please keep these young women in your prayers as they continue to listen the lord's voice in their lives. in the gospel, jesus reminds us of the two great co mmandments: to love god with all our heart and to love our neighbour as ourselves. in many ways, both of these invitations are reflected in what we do as a parish. we show our love for god by being open to his call, and our love for one another through our prayers, o ur care and our remembrance of those who have gone before us. whether we are discerning what god wants of us, pra ying for someone we love, or simply offering a little kindness to another person, we ar living out those two great commandments. may november be a month of prayer, remembrance and renewed trust in god's love. st colmcilles
